technical_and_design_decisions: Development will adhere to the Mule ESB kernel architecture and Java-based extension guidelines.
Domain lifecycle features (U1) and DeploymentService property overrides (U2) will extend Mule's core deployment management APIs.
AMQP transport implementation (U4-U8) will be based on AMQP 0-9-1 specification using a standard Java client (e.g., RabbitMQ Client library).
An XML Schema Definition (XSD) will be authored for the AMQP namespace to support Spring/Mule configuration parsing, validation, and IDE autocompletion.
Inbound continuous consumption (U7) will be implemented using a dedicated MessageReceiver listening asynchronously on AMQP queues, converting AMQP messages to MuleEvents.
Instant consumption (U8) will be implemented using a MessageRequester pattern for synchronous, on-demand fetching of single messages during flow execution.
assumptions: The developer has existing expertise in Java, Mule ESB core architecture, and AMQP protocols.
An AMQP broker (e.g., RabbitMQ) is readily available for integration testing.
Community spec review (U3) involves producing technical documentation/draft spec and incorporating feedback within the iteration.
Effort estimates assume standard 8-hour workdays and include design, implementation, unit testing, and developer integration testing.

activities.activity_description: Implement API capabilities to deploy a domain, undeploy a domain along with all associated applications, and redeploy/update domain applications dynamically.
Extend DeploymentService to accept application configuration property overrides at deployment time and pass them into the application execution context.

activities.activity_name: AMQP Transport Specification & XSD Schema Creation (U3, U4)
activities.activity_description: Draft technical specification for community review and design the XML Schema (XSD) defining AMQP connectors, endpoints, and transaction elements for IDE validation/autocomplete.

activities.activity_name: AMQP Transport Skeleton & Global Configuration (U5, U6)
activities.activity_description: Create base project structure and implement global AMQP connector configuration allowing single-point management of connection parameters, channels, and common attributes.
Develop the AMQP Message Receiver to continuously consume queue messages, convert payloads/metadata into MuleEvent objects, and dispatch them to Mule flows.
Develop the AMQP Message Requester component allowing synchronous, mid-flow polling and retrieval of AMQP messages.
Perform end-to-end testing with an active AMQP broker, test domain lifecycle scenarios, write usage documentation, and resolve defects across all features.
